audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4, 5 and 6 were marked Skill / Jayce / Jayce while the why-text on those exact rows says the opposite: whys[4] calls level 6 a kill he can't escape, whys[5] says first item makes every root a full combo and 'you out-trade', whys[6] says you stay the relevant teamfight threat.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Neeko / Skill / Neeko for those rows and the win rate is 62.96%. The chart was arguing against its own paragraphs and against the data.
audit.corrected: Row 4 -> Neeko (4/10 -> 7/10), row 5 -> Skill, row 6 -> Neeko (5/10 -> 6/10), as matched full/content pairs in one atomic group. Rows 0-3 already match the packet and stay.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike — the single most important timing on this page — was sold as 'set R while invisible from W'.
audit.why: Riot's Shapesplitter text has no invisibility: third-attack magic damage, a brief move speed gain, and a directional clone. The mechanic that makes this spike real is Inherent Glamour, which Riot states hides the Pop Blossom preparation. Against a champion who only has to walk backwards to answer the ult, a hidden wind-up is the whole spike; a nonexistent invisibility is a player standing still in the open.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text, mid and wants.you[1] rebuilt on the disguise and the hidden preparation, with Thundering Blow's 20s cooldown as the window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stance swap is never named as a burst tell — the page treats his damage as poke only.
audit.why: _missing flags autoreset-burst-tell. Riot's R text: swapping into Mercury Cannon makes his first attack in that form reduce the target's armour and magic resist, and the swap itself is on a 6s cooldown with a move speed gain from Hextech Capacitor. The swap animation is the cue to leave; by the time the shred attack lands the combo is already on you.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[2] alongside the knockback.

audit.why: The page's treatment of Thundering Blow as the thing that breaks up a Neeko commit matches Riot's Hammer-stance E text (magic damage and a knockback), and it is correctly identified as his only disengage. Added its real number rather than changing the claim.
audit.corrected: 20s at rank 1 written into spikes[1].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast is described as 'gate-accelerated poke' with no explanation of what the gate does or when he is punishable.
audit.why: Acceleration Gate is a separate cast (Cannon-stance E); firing Shock Blast through it increases missile speed, range and damage. Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 dropping to 6s. Knowing the gate is a second cast is what lets a player recognise the empowered version before it is fired.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and report[5].t now name Acceleration Gate and what it does to the missile.

edits.before: Q + E is your first threat, but his E-knockback cancels your combo and his poke still out-ranges you, so he keeps the level.
edits.after: Q + E is your first threat, but Thundering Blow knocks you out of the combo and his swap-attack shred lands first, so he keeps the level.

edits.before: Pop Blossom set unseen via W invisibility or disguise turns a landed E into a stun-combo kill he can't escape with no sustain.
edits.after: Pop Blossom wound up under a disguise, where the preparation is hidden, turns a landed E into a stun combo he has no sustain to survive.

edits.before: Pop Blossom is your takeover: set R while invisible from W or disguised, walk into his face on his E-knockback cooldown, and the stun-into-Q deletes a squishy Jayce.
edits.after: Pop Blossom is your takeover: wind it up disguised so the preparation stays hidden, walk in while Thundering Blow is down on its 20s, and the stun-into-Q deletes him.

edits.before: Six is where this flips hard in your favor. Pop Blossom is the equalizer — pop W to go invisible or wear a disguise, drift toward him while he's poking, and slam down for the stun. A landed E-root into Q-rebloom and the R stun is a near-guaranteed kill on his squishy frame, and he has no sustain to recover. Bait his E-knockback first (it's his only disengage), then commit. Through Levels 4-5 before ult, keep farming with Q waveclear and don't all-in — that window is even at best.
edits.after: Six is where this flips hard in your favor. Pop Blossom is the equalizer — wear a disguise so the wind-up never shows, drift toward him while he's poking, and slam down for the stun. A landed E-root into Q-rebloom and the R stun is a near-guaranteed kill on his squishy frame, and he has no sustain to recover. Bait Thundering Blow first — 20s at rank 1, and his only disengage — then commit. Through Levels 4-5 keep farming with Q waveclear and don't all-in; that window is even at best.

edits.before: Reach Level 6 and set R unseen via W invisibility or disguise so the stun lands before he stance-swaps away
edits.after: Reach Level 6 and wind up R under a disguise, where it stays hidden, so the stun lands before he swaps out

edits.before: Gate-accelerated poke — stand behind minions and close after it whiffs. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Shock Blast fired through his own gate is the poke — stand behind minions and close in the window after it whiffs.

edits.before: Track Jayce’s Shock Blast: Gate-accelerated poke — stand behind minions and close after it whiffs. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Shock Blast: fired through Acceleration Gate it gains speed, range and damage. Stand behind minions, step up once it whiffs.

notes: The full layer never names a single Jayce ability beyond Shock Blast, which the packet flags as a defect — Thundering Blow, Acceleration Gate, Hyper Charge and the Mercury Cannon/Hammer swap all go unmentioned there even though the content layer uses them. Most of those strings are shared boilerplate ('Take extended auto wars at his range', 'That is Jayce's rehearsed moment') that would need rewriting as a set rather than one at a time. Separately, this page and its mirror both describe the armour/MR shred correctly only in the content layer; the mirror's note that the shred is the first attack after swapping INTO Mercury Cannon (not the Hammer hit) is worth keeping consistent if anyone rewrites the full layer.
